annotations.title: Add a race we do not list

description: Put a race search_races does not list (a trail race, a road marathon, a local event, anything) on the user's Goal Race list, the same list save_race writes to. Search first; use this only when the race is not in the results. A race the site does list still goes in as that race (linked to its page, with the status and format you pass), and the result says so in listed_race: tell the user. A date is required: a race without one has no place on a calendar. When the organiser has not announced it, ask the user for their best guess and pass date_confirmed: false — the race then goes in with status 'monitoring', and nothing writes 'TBC' into the title. status is one of wishlist, registered, monitoring, booking, estimating: 'wishlist' by default, 'registered' when the user has already signed up. A race already on the user's list (get_calendar shows it) is changed with update_race, not added again. One race per call. All dates are the user's local calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD) in their own time zone. Requires signing in.

date_confirmed.description: False when the date is the user's guess rather than the organiser's announcement. Default true.

format.description: Wave or distance the user picked, e.g. '42K'. Omit when they did not say.

location.description: Town and country, e.g. 'Chamonix, France'. Omit when unknown.

not_listed.description: Only after this tool answered with a listed race the user says is a different one: true adds the race as typed. Leave out otherwise.

status.description: 'wishlist': On the list, not signed up. The default. 'registered': Signed up and paid. 'monitoring': Watching it: the date or the registration is not settled yet. 'booking': Booking travel and beds for it. 'estimating': Working out what it will cost.

title.description: Race name as the user says it, year included if they said it. Max 200 chars. No 'TBC'.

url.description: The organiser's page, absolute http(s) url. Omit when unknown.
